title: Netflix Takes on YouTube by Licensing Digital Publisher Videos Starting August

body:
Netflix is making its boldest move yet to capture the kind of casual, always-on viewing that YouTube has dominated for over a decade. Starting August 3, the streaming giant will begin licensing videos from popular digital publishers — bringing home tours, recipe clips, celebrity interviews, and short-form content directly to its platform. This strategic pivot could significantly impact how Indian diaspora audiences consume content, potentially offering a new avenue for diverse, snackable entertainment alongside their existing subscriptions.

> **"The licensed content ranges from three-minute clips to episodes past twenty minutes.

None of these videos are produced by Netflix."** https://x.com/NetflixIndia/status/2078110146597957905 https://youtube.com/watch?v=VtlrAlqo9u0

What's Coming

Netflix has partnered with BuzzFeed Studios, Condé Nast titles including Vogue and Vanity Fair, Hearst Magazines brands like Elle and Cosmopolitan, and Penske Media outlets such as Variety and Rolling Stone. The licensed content ranges from three-minute clips to episodes past twenty minutes.

None of these videos are produced by Netflix. The company is licensing existing series that already have loyal audiences on YouTube — Architectural Digest's home tours, Bon Appétit's cooking videos, and Vanity Fair's celebrity lie detector tests. This move, set to roll out in early August, aims to diversify Netflix's content library without the high production costs associated with original series.
